rows.definition: The one following this. Next assumes an order and a place already occupied.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A position that only exists because something else already claimed this one — next has no meaning without an order already in place.
rows.historical_meaning: Old English niehst (nighest, nearest), the superlative of neah (nigh, near); the one following this.

rows.definition: A point where many connections bind together. From the Latin for binding — a nexus is a knot rather than a place.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A knot rather than a location — what makes a nexus a nexus is how many things are bound there, not where it happens to sit.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin nexus (a binding, a connection), the past participle of nectere (to bind, to tie); a point where many connections bind together.

rows.definition: A compound fragment meaning a name index. Not an English word; flagged for the mis-cut band.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A fragment stitched from name and index, kept in the record honestly as a cut rather than passed off as a coined term.

rows.definition: The machine handling of human language. A named field rather than a concept.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The named discipline of teaching a machine to handle what people actually say, rather than a general idea about language.
rows.historical_meaning: An acronym for natural language processing, each word tracing to Latin: natura (birth, inborn character), lingua (tongue, hence language), and processus (a going-forward), from procedere; the machine handling of human language.

rows.definition: Refusal, or absence. The shortest complete sentence, and a full answer on its own.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The shortest sentence the house has, and a complete one — nothing else needs to be said for a no to stand on its own.
rows.historical_meaning: Old English na, a compound of ne (not) plus a (ever) — literally not ever — worn down into the general negative particle.

rows.definition: Holding to what is right when nothing compels it. Nobility here is a description of conduct, not of rank.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Conduct rather than lineage — what a word for birth came to mean once the house decided rank was never the point.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin nobilis (well-known, notable, of high birth), from (g)noscere (to know); holding to what is right when nothing compels it, a word for conduct that outgrew its claim about rank.

rows.definition: A point where connections meet. A node's meaning comes from its edges rather than from itself.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A point that means nothing alone — whatever a node is, it borrows entirely from the edges tied to it.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin nodus (a knot); a point where connections meet, its meaning drawn from the edges tied to it rather than from anything held inside.

rows.definition: Nomos (Greek νόμος: law, custom, that which is apportioned and held to — the law as a THING a house can point at). The policy document turned into columns: sections, subsections, the tables inside them and the date the document itself states, as DATA with no opinion about how any of it looks. DISTINCT FROM RENDERING, and the distinction is the whole reason it exists apart: a renderer takes structure and puts it on a screen, and this takes prose somebody wrote and finds the structure already in it. THE DATE IS THE DOCUMENT'S OR IT IS EMPTY — never a default, because a page printing a hardcoded date for a document that does not carry one is telling the reader something the document never said; both of the house's labels are read, "Last updated:" and "Effective date:". A TABLE IS LIFTED, NOT FLATTENED: a markdown table inside a section comes back as headers and rows on that section. NESTING IS KEPT and the tree is the document's own. NOTHING THROWS AND NOTHING IS INVENTED: an empty document, a document with no headings, a heading with no body, a subheading with no parent, a table outside any section, a header-less table and a ragged table all come back as calm shapes, and what the document does not say the parse does not say either. It parses a shape, not a language — lists, links, emphasis and code fences ride through as raw text, and only two heading levels nest. No clock, no disk, no network, no DOM, zero imports; reading the file stays the caller's business.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The policy document turned into columns: sections, subsections, the tables inside them and the date the document itself states, as data with no opinion about how any of it looks.
rows.historical_meaning: Greek nomos (law, custom, that which is apportioned), from nemein (to distribute, to hold as one's own); law understood as a thing a house can point to and read.

rows.definition: Not. A part placed at the front to deny what follows.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The plainest denial the house has — a single syllable placed in front to undo whatever comes after it.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin non (not), from an earlier ne oinom, literally not one; a part placed at the front to deny whatever follows it.

rows.definition: Outside version control — ground git does not watch; named so the unwatched is never mistaken for the recorded.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Ground deliberately marked as unwatched, so nothing there is ever mistaken for something the record actually kept.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin non (not) compounded with git, the version-control system named in 2005 after British slang for an unpleasant person, chosen self-deprecatingly; ground outside what that tool watches.

rows.definition: The arctic-blue theme family — cold light over quiet fjords, worn by editors; the name enters as itself.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A named theme rather than a translated idea — the word for north arrives whole, carrying its own cold light rather than standing for a concept.
rows.historical_meaning: Old Norse nordr (north), the same Germanic root that gives English north; French and other Romance languages took this Germanic word for the direction from seafaring contact, standing alongside rather than replacing Latin's own septentrio, aquilo and boreas.

rows.definition: To bring differing things into one common form. Normalisation makes comparison possible and loses what was particular.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The trade a house makes for comparison — everything measured against the same square, and whatever was particular about each thing quietly given up for it.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin norma (a carpenter's square, a pattern, a rule), with the -izare ending (to make into); to bring differing things into one common form, measured against the same square.

rows.definition: The direction toward the pole. One of the four bearings, and the one maps are conventionally oriented to.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The bearing every map quietly agrees to put at the top, more by convention than by any fact about the direction itself.
rows.historical_meaning: Old English nord, from Proto-Germanic *nurtra-, of uncertain deeper origin — perhaps related to a root for left, since the direction sits to the left of someone facing the rising sun.

rows.definition: Of or toward the north. A bearing made into a description of a region.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A bearing that stopped pointing and started describing — north turned into a way of naming a whole region rather than just a direction from it.
rows.historical_meaning: Old English nord (north) with the directional suffix -erne; a bearing made into a description of a region.

rows.definition: The reversal of what follows. The word that turns an assertion into its denial.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The single word standing between a claim and its opposite — say it, and everything after flips.
rows.historical_meaning: Old English nawiht (not anything, nothing at all), a compound of ne (not) plus a (ever) plus wiht (a thing), later worn down to not; the word that turns an assertion into its own denial.

rows.definition: A short record set down so it is not lost. Also a single sounded pitch.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Something small marked down so it survives — whether a thought caught before it slips or a single pitch held long enough to be named.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin nota (a mark, a sign, a written character), from noscere (to know); a short record set down so it is not lost, or a single sounded pitch marked the same way.

rows.definition: A message sent to make someone aware of something now. It interrupts on purpose, which is why it must be worth it.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: An interruption that has to earn its place — sent only because something is judged worth breaking attention for right now.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin notificare (to make known), from notus (known, from noscere) plus facere (to make); a message sent to make someone aware of something now.

rows.definition: The present moment, which is the only one anything can be done in. Now is never a duration.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The one moment where anything can actually be done — not a stretch of time, just the single edge where action is even possible.
rows.historical_meaning: Old English nu, from the Proto-Indo-European particle *nu (now); the present moment, the only one anything can actually be done in.

rows.definition: To destroy entirely rather than repair. A deliberate total removal, named for its bluntness.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: The bluntest word in the house for removal — nothing partial about it, and no attempt at repair implied.
rows.historical_meaning: Clipped from nuclear, Latin nucleus (a little nut, a kernel), from nux (nut); military slang for atomic weapons since the mid-twentieth century, generalised since to any deliberate, total removal.

rows.definition: Permitted to hold nothing. Nullability makes absence a valid state rather than an error.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Permission granted in advance for a field to hold nothing at all — absence treated as a valid answer rather than a failure.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin nullus (none, not any), from ne (not) plus ullus (any); permitted to hold nothing, which makes absence a valid state.

rows.definition: A count or a measure, held as a value. A number carries no meaning until someone says what it counted.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A value that means nothing on its own — a number only becomes information once something says what was actually counted.
rows.historical_meaning: Old French nombre, from Latin numerus (a number, a sum); a count or a measure held as a value.

rows.definition: A thing considered as a thing, apart from what it does. Also whatever an action is aimed at.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A thing regarded for what it is rather than for what it does, or whatever a verb has taken aim at — the same word answering to both.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin objectum (a thing thrown or placed before), from ob- (against, before) plus jacere (to throw); a thing considered apart from what it does, or whatever an action is aimed at.

rows.definition: Attentive looking that records what is there. Observation is meant to change the observer and not the observed.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: Watching meant to leave its subject untouched and change only the one doing the watching.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin observatio, from observare (to watch, to keep, to guard), from ob- (before) plus servare (to keep, to watch); attentive looking that records what is there.

rows.definition: A place built for watching what is far away. An observatory changes nothing it studies.
rows.sanctuary_meaning: A place built entirely for watching, never for touching — everything studied stays exactly as it was found.
rows.historical_meaning: Latin observatio (a watching, a keeping), with the place-suffix -orium; a place built for watching what is far away.
